goal: Reliably search and synthesize grounded, wikilink-cited literature answers from an external Knowledge Base directory on Windows without script crashes.

trials.organic_prompt: I am writing a literature review section on how All-Star awards affect financial analyst performance. Search my local knowledge base in ./library and summarize the mechanisms, empirical findings (exact variables and magnitudes), and key operational proxies with wikilink citations. Remember the library path for future questions in this workspace.

Look up Outside Opportunities in my knowledge base under ./library and do a deep dive into how it is measured across papers, including the exact paper variable names, canonical wiki variable names, formulas, and empirical results on compensation and pay-for-luck.

Search my knowledge base in ./library for formal theoretical results on market informational efficiency and the equilibrium proportion of informed traders. Summarize the main theorems, model parameters (with symbols), and any gaps if a topic is not covered.

rubric.description: Every empirical magnitude, formula, theorem, and symbol matches the files in ./library with zero fabricated claims.
Uses valid Obsidian [[wikilink]] citations and preserves both canonical wiki variable names and exact paper variable names.
Resolves and persists the external KB path cleanly (.kb_root when asked), executes search/deep-graph workflow without broken script failures, and covers linked pages thoroughly.
Delivers a concise, well-structured synthesis with a Sources Consulted list and appropriate follow-up save suggestion when warranted.
